title: Target the installed v4 version
instruction: Check package manifests, the lockfile, and installed types before choosing an API. Use supported v4 exports.
exceptions: Use the project lockfile and installed exports as the final API authority. Do not upgrade dependencies as an incidental rule fix.

title: Replace removed APIs
instruction: Replace removed or renamed APIs using the migration map for the installed version. Do not copy v3 examples unchanged.
exceptions: Use the project lockfile and installed exports as the final API authority. Do not upgrade dependencies as an incidental rule fix.

title: Use integrated Schema and Match
instruction: Import Schema and Match from the v4 effect package instead of obsolete standalone packages.
exceptions: Use the project lockfile and installed exports as the final API authority. Do not upgrade dependencies as an incidental rule fix.

title: Use current platform imports
instruction: Use FileSystem and Path from effect. Use the installed v4 HTTP, process, crypto, and runtime exports.
exceptions: Use the project lockfile and installed exports as the final API authority. Do not upgrade dependencies as an incidental rule fix.

title: Verify uncertain APIs
instruction: Inspect the installed declaration or authoritative source when an API is uncertain. Do not invent an export, signature, or error type.
exceptions: Use the project lockfile and installed exports as the final API authority. Do not upgrade dependencies as an incidental rule fix.

title: Preserve dependency decisions
instruction: Keep existing dependency versions and package-manager conventions. Propose a separate upgrade when a required capability is unavailable.
exceptions: Use the project lockfile and installed exports as the final API authority. Do not upgrade dependencies as an incidental rule fix.

title: Use FileSystem
instruction: Read, write, inspect, copy, remove, and enumerate files through the FileSystem service.
exceptions: Exclude platform adapters and application startup from the configured scope. Preserve required platform-specific path behavior.

title: Avoid blocking filesystem calls
instruction: Keep synchronous filesystem I/O out of business code. Wrapping a blocking Node operation in Effect.sync does not make it nonblocking.
exceptions: Exclude platform adapters and application startup from the configured scope. Preserve required platform-specific path behavior.

title: Use the Path service
instruction: Use the injected Path service for platform-dependent path operations. Make POSIX or Windows-specific semantics explicit.
exceptions: Exclude platform adapters and application startup from the configured scope. Preserve required platform-specific path behavior.

title: Scope filesystem resources
instruction: Use scoped file handles and scoped temporary resources when their lifetime belongs to the operation. Close or remove resources on interruption.
exceptions: Exclude platform adapters and application startup from the configured scope. Preserve required platform-specific path behavior.

title: Stream file changes and content
instruction: Use FileSystem stream and watch operations when processing incremental content or changes. Keep consumption bounded.
exceptions: Exclude platform adapters and application startup from the configured scope. Preserve required platform-specific path behavior.

title: Use terminal services
instruction: Use Terminal for interactive input and output. Keep machine-readable command output separate from application logs.
exceptions: Exclude platform adapters and application startup from the configured scope. Preserve required platform-specific path behavior.

title: Use HttpClient
instruction: Use an injected Effect HttpClient for HTTP requests instead of global fetch or direct Node HTTP calls.
exceptions: A required vendor SDK may remain behind an injected adapter. Preserve status handling, streaming, retry, and cancellation behavior when migrating.

title: Prefer the existing Effect HTTP stack
instruction: Use existing Effect HTTP capabilities before adding another HTTP client. Put unavoidable vendor clients behind a service.
exceptions: A required vendor SDK may remain behind an injected adapter. Preserve status handling, streaming, retry, and cancellation behavior when migrating.

title: Choose status handling explicitly
instruction: Specify which HTTP status codes count as success or typed failure. Do not assume transport success implies application success.
exceptions: A required vendor SDK may remain behind an injected adapter. Preserve status handling, streaming, retry, and cancellation behavior when migrating.

title: Decode response boundaries
instruction: Decode external response bodies with a Schema. Keep transport, parsing, and domain validation errors distinguishable.
exceptions: A required vendor SDK may remain behind an injected adapter. Preserve status handling, streaming, retry, and cancellation behavior when migrating.

title: Own response resources
instruction: Consume response bodies in the lifetime required by the HTTP API. Do not leak a response stream past its resource scope.
exceptions: A required vendor SDK may remain behind an injected adapter. Preserve status handling, streaming, retry, and cancellation behavior when migrating.

title: Preserve request policies
instruction: Define timeout and retry behavior deliberately. Retry only operations and failures for which repeating work is safe.
exceptions: A required vendor SDK may remain behind an injected adapter. Preserve status handling, streaming, retry, and cancellation behavior when migrating.

title: Use ChildProcess
instruction: Describe subprocesses with the installed v4 ChildProcess API and execute them through ChildProcessSpawner.
exceptions: Low-level platform operations without an equivalent belong in adapters. Command argument and environment semantics must remain unchanged.

title: Prefer explicit argument arrays
instruction: Pass command arguments as separate values. Use a shell only when shell semantics are required and inputs are handled safely.
exceptions: Low-level platform operations without an equivalent belong in adapters. Command argument and environment semantics must remain unchanged.

title: Inject process execution
instruction: Expose subprocess execution through an injected service. Business modules should not start a global process executor.
exceptions: Low-level platform operations without an equivalent belong in adapters. Command argument and environment semantics must remain unchanged.

title: Stream subprocess output
instruction: Consume potentially large subprocess output incrementally with Stream or Sink. Choose a bounded collection limit when collecting.
exceptions: Low-level platform operations without an equivalent belong in adapters. Command argument and environment semantics must remain unchanged.

title: Keep exit decisions at startup
instruction: Return typed outcomes from business code. Application startup owns exit status, shutdown, and signal handling.
exceptions: Low-level platform operations without an equivalent belong in adapters. Command argument and environment semantics must remain unchanged.

title: Require a real replacement
instruction: Restrict Node APIs that have suitable Effect replacements. For unmatched capabilities, define an adapter instead of inventing an Effect equivalent.
exceptions: Low-level platform operations without an equivalent belong in adapters. Command argument and environment semantics must remain unchanged.

title: Sleep with Effect
instruction: Use Effect.sleep for interruptible waiting. Do not implement sleeps with timers or Promise constructors.
exceptions: Pure conversion of an existing timestamp may stay pure. Preserve wall-clock versus monotonic-time semantics, schedule timing, and time zones.

title: Schedule repeated work
instruction: Use Schedule and Effect repetition for recurring jobs. Specify fixed-rate versus spaced timing deliberately.
exceptions: Pure conversion of an existing timestamp may stay pure. Preserve wall-clock versus monotonic-time semantics, schedule timing, and time zones.

title: Compose retries
instruction: Use Effect.retry with an explicit Schedule or retry policy. Bound attempts or elapsed time where required.
exceptions: Pure conversion of an existing timestamp may stay pure. Preserve wall-clock versus monotonic-time semantics, schedule timing, and time zones.

title: Read time through Clock
instruction: Get current time through Clock or the corresponding Effect time API so tests can control it.
exceptions: Pure conversion of an existing timestamp may stay pure. Preserve wall-clock versus monotonic-time semantics, schedule timing, and time zones.

title: Use DateTime for date operations
instruction: Use DateTime for domain date and time calculations when its semantics fit. Make time-zone and calendar assumptions explicit.
exceptions: Pure conversion of an existing timestamp may stay pure. Preserve wall-clock versus monotonic-time semantics, schedule timing, and time zones.

title: Make duration units explicit
instruction: Represent durations with Duration constructors or supported unit-bearing literals. Avoid unexplained numeric time constants.
exceptions: Pure conversion of an existing timestamp may stay pure. Preserve wall-clock versus monotonic-time semantics, schedule timing, and time zones.

title: Use Random for ordinary randomness
instruction: Use the Random service for ordinary random choices instead of Math.random.
exceptions: Ordinary seeded Random is not cryptographically secure. Verify SecureRandom operations and layer requirements against the installed v4 package.

title: Use appropriate random operations
instruction: Use Random operations with documented integer-range and shuffle semantics. Check whether bounds are inclusive or exclusive.
exceptions: Ordinary seeded Random is not cryptographically secure. Verify SecureRandom operations and layer requirements against the installed v4 package.

title: Use SecureRandom for UUIDs
instruction: Use SecureRandom from effect/crypto for secure UUID generation when the installed version supports the needed format.
exceptions: Ordinary seeded Random is not cryptographically secure. Verify SecureRandom operations and layer requirements against the installed v4 package.

title: Keep security guarantees
instruction: Use a cryptographically secure source for tokens, secrets, and security-sensitive identifiers. Never replace it with seeded Random.
exceptions: Ordinary seeded Random is not cryptographically secure. Verify SecureRandom operations and layer requirements against the installed v4 package.

title: Control randomness in tests
instruction: Provide a deterministic Random seed or test service for ordinary randomness. Keep security-sensitive test doubles explicit.
exceptions: Ordinary seeded Random is not cryptographically secure. Verify SecureRandom operations and layer requirements against the installed v4 package.

title: Adapt unmatched crypto operations
instruction: Use an Effect crypto operation only when algorithm, encoding, timing, and security properties match. Put unmatched native crypto behind an adapter.
exceptions: Ordinary seeded Random is not cryptographically secure. Verify SecureRandom operations and layer requirements against the installed v4 package.

title: Read configuration through Config

exceptions: Configuration bootstrap adapters may read the host environment. Decode missing, malformed, and empty values according to explicit application requirements.

title: Validate configuration types
instruction: Decode and validate configuration at its boundary with Config and Schema rather than spreading ad hoc parsing through business logic.
exceptions: Configuration bootstrap adapters may read the host environment. Decode missing, malformed, and empty values according to explicit application requirements.

title: Make defaults intentional
instruction: Mark required settings explicitly. Add defaults only when missing configuration genuinely has a valid meaning.
exceptions: Configuration bootstrap adapters may read the host environment. Decode missing, malformed, and empty values according to explicit application requirements.

title: Redact secrets
instruction: Represent sensitive configuration as Redacted values. Keep the wrapper until the external boundary needs the secret.
exceptions: Configuration bootstrap adapters may read the host environment. Decode missing, malformed, and empty values according to explicit application requirements.

title: Limit secret access
instruction: Unwrap a Redacted value only at a necessary boundary. Keep secrets out of logs, traces, errors, and diagnostic messages.
exceptions: Configuration bootstrap adapters may read the host environment. Decode missing, malformed, and empty values according to explicit application requirements.

title: Replace providers in tests
instruction: Provide test configuration through ConfigProvider. Avoid changing global process.env to control business tests.
exceptions: Configuration bootstrap adapters may read the host environment. Decode missing, malformed, and empty values according to explicit application requirements.

title: Use Effect logging

exceptions: Human-facing terminal output and protocol output are not application logs. Avoid adding spans to tiny pure helpers or high-cardinality metric labels.

title: Keep output channels separate
instruction: Use Console or Terminal for intentional user output. Keep logs separate from JSON, binary, or other machine-readable output.
exceptions: Human-facing terminal output and protocol output are not application logs. Avoid adding spans to tiny pure helpers or high-cardinality metric labels.

title: Attach structured context
instruction: Attach stable structured log annotations for relevant identifiers. Do not encode every field into a free-form message.
exceptions: Human-facing terminal output and protocol output are not application logs. Avoid adding spans to tiny pure helpers or high-cardinality metric labels.

title: Trace meaningful operations
instruction: Use named Effect.fn functions or spans for meaningful business and I/O operations. Preserve context across service calls.
exceptions: Human-facing terminal output and protocol output are not application logs. Avoid adding spans to tiny pure helpers or high-cardinality metric labels.

title: Use Effect metrics
instruction: Record counters, durations, and other metrics through Effect Metric operations. Reuse metric definitions and control label cardinality.
exceptions: Human-facing terminal output and protocol output are not application logs. Avoid adding spans to tiny pure helpers or high-cardinality metric labels.

title: Return Effect from effectful business APIs

title: Keep pure code simple

exceptions: Pure helpers may return plain values. Promise-only framework callbacks and third-party adapters may use their required foreign types when excluded from the configured scope.

title: Defer side effects
instruction: Do not execute a side effect while constructing Effect.succeed or at module initialization. Put execution in a lazy Effect constructor.
exceptions: Pure helpers may return plain values. Promise-only framework callbacks and third-party adapters may use their required foreign types when excluded from the configured scope.

title: Choose synchronous constructors correctly
instruction: Use Effect.sync for deferred operations whose thrown exceptions are defects. Use Effect.try with a typed catch mapping for expected exceptions.
exceptions: Pure helpers may return plain values. Promise-only framework callbacks and third-party adapters may use their required foreign types when excluded from the configured scope.

title: Choose Promise constructors correctly
instruction: Use Effect.tryPromise with a typed catch mapping for expected rejection. Use Effect.promise only when rejection should be treated as a defect.
exceptions: Pure helpers may return plain values. Promise-only framework callbacks and third-party adapters may use their required foreign types when excluded from the configured scope.

title: Bridge cancellation deliberately
instruction: Create foreign work lazily inside the Effect callback. Pass the provided AbortSignal when supported, and register callback cleanup without claiming that uncancellable work becomes cancellable.
exceptions: Pure helpers may return plain values. Promise-only framework callbacks and third-party adapters may use their required foreign types when excluded from the configured scope.

title: Use discriminated expected errors
instruction: Represent expected failures with useful tagged error types such as Data.TaggedError or Schema.TaggedError. Include actionable context.
exceptions: Invariant violations may be defects. Intentional recovery is allowed when the failure contract and interruption behavior remain correct.

title: Fail through the error channel
instruction: Use Effect.fail or a supported yieldable error for expected business failure. Do not use thrown exceptions as the normal business failure path.
exceptions: Invariant violations may be defects. Intentional recovery is allowed when the failure contract and interruption behavior remain correct.

title: Preserve error information
instruction: Map foreign errors to domain errors while retaining the useful cause and context. Do not erase the original error with a generic string.
exceptions: Invariant violations may be defects. Intentional recovery is allowed when the failure contract and interruption behavior remain correct.

title: Recover selectively
instruction: Use catchTag, catchTags, or an appropriate conditional catch for specific expected failures. Preserve unmatched failures.
exceptions: Invariant violations may be defects. Intentional recovery is allowed when the failure contract and interruption behavior remain correct.

title: Keep defects distinct
instruction: Do not convert all expected failures to defects with orDie. Use fatal failure only when the application contract really treats it as unrecoverable.
exceptions: Invariant violations may be defects. Intentional recovery is allowed when the failure contract and interruption behavior remain correct.

title: Preserve cancellation
instruction: When handling Cause, distinguish interruption from recoverable failure. Do not accidentally swallow interruption or convert cancellation into successful work.
exceptions: Invariant violations may be defects. Intentional recovery is allowed when the failure contract and interruption behavior remain correct.

title: Compose concurrent work with Effect
instruction: Use Effect.all or Effect.forEach rather than Promise fan-out for Effect-based operations.
exceptions: Effect.all and Effect.forEach are sequential by default. Fixed finite parallel work and application-owned detached fibers need explicit lifetime decisions.

title: Bound growing concurrency
instruction: Set a deliberate concurrency limit for input-dependent fan-out. Keep sequential execution when required; missing concurrency is not automatically unbounded.
exceptions: Effect.all and Effect.forEach are sequential by default. Fixed finite parallel work and application-owned detached fibers need explicit lifetime decisions.

title: Choose race semantics
instruction: Distinguish first completion from first success before replacing Promise.race or Promise.any. Ensure losing work is cancelled when supported.
exceptions: Effect.all and Effect.forEach are sequential by default. Fixed finite parallel work and application-owned detached fibers need explicit lifetime decisions.

title: Own fiber lifetimes
instruction: Choose forkChild, forkScoped, or an explicit Scope according to the owner. Use forkDetach only for intentionally application-owned background work.
exceptions: Effect.all and Effect.forEach are sequential by default. Fixed finite parallel work and application-owned detached fibers need explicit lifetime decisions.

title: Handle background outcomes
instruction: Retain, join, interrupt, or observe fibers as required. Define how background failure and application shutdown are handled.
exceptions: Effect.all and Effect.forEach are sequential by default. Fixed finite parallel work and application-owned detached fibers need explicit lifetime decisions.

title: Compose instead of starting runtimes
instruction: Inside business Effects, yield or combine Effects instead of calling Effect.run operations. Runtime execution belongs to an explicit foreign boundary.
exceptions: Effect.all and Effect.forEach are sequential by default. Fixed finite parallel work and application-owned detached fibers need explicit lifetime decisions.

title: Pair acquisition and release
instruction: Use acquireRelease, acquireUseRelease, or acquireDisposable for owned resources as appropriate. Define acquisition failure behavior.
exceptions: Exclude application entry points and framework bridges from the configured scope. A truly pure synchronous constructor can use its documented safe or Unsafe API when its preconditions are proved.

title: Close the owning Scope
instruction: Open and close Scope at the owner of the resource lifetime. Do not remove Scope requirements with a cast.
exceptions: Exclude application entry points and framework bridges from the configured scope. A truly pure synchronous constructor can use its documented safe or Unsafe API when its preconditions are proved.

title: Clean up on every exit
instruction: Register finalizers so normal completion, failure, and interruption release resources. Avoid leaking resources when acquisition partially succeeds.
exceptions: Exclude application entry points and framework bridges from the configured scope. A truly pure synchronous constructor can use its documented safe or Unsafe API when its preconditions are proved.

title: Keep resources inside their lifetime
instruction: Do not return or store a scoped resource for use after its owner has closed. Extend the owner scope instead.
exceptions: Exclude application entry points and framework bridges from the configured scope. A truly pure synchronous constructor can use its documented safe or Unsafe API when its preconditions are proved.

title: Use the platform entry point
instruction: For a standalone application, run the main Effect with the correct platform runMain so shutdown and interruption are handled.
exceptions: Exclude application entry points and framework bridges from the configured scope. A truly pure synchronous constructor can use its documented safe or Unsafe API when its preconditions are proved.

title: Centralize foreign runtime bridges
instruction: Integrate Promise-only frameworks at a dedicated adapter or entry point. Reuse the intended application context and dispose its lifetime correctly.
exceptions: Exclude application entry points and framework bridges from the configured scope. A truly pure synchronous constructor can use its documented safe or Unsafe API when its preconditions are proved.

title: Inject replaceable dependencies
instruction: Model external and replaceable dependencies as v4 Context.Service identifiers with stable keys.
exceptions: Small pure helpers do not need services. Per-request resources are valid when request ownership is explicit rather than accidental.

title: Construct implementations with Layer
instruction: Use Layer to construct service implementations and their dependencies. Keep live and test implementations replaceable.
exceptions: Small pure helpers do not need services. Per-request resources are valid when request ownership is explicit rather than accidental.

title: Hide implementation requirements
instruction: Capture implementation-only dependencies when building a service. Do not leak them from every public service method.
exceptions: Small pure helpers do not need services. Per-request resources are valid when request ownership is explicit rather than accidental.

title: Compose layer dependencies correctly
instruction: Use dependency-providing operations when one Layer requires another. Layer merge alone does not supply one sibling to another.
exceptions: Small pure helpers do not need services. Per-request resources are valid when request ownership is explicit rather than accidental.

title: Choose sharing deliberately
instruction: Reuse Layer values when memoized sharing is intended. Use fresh construction only when an independent instance is required.
exceptions: Small pure helpers do not need services. Per-request resources are valid when request ownership is explicit rather than accidental.

title: Provide at the composition boundary

exceptions: Small pure helpers do not need services. Per-request resources are valid when request ownership is explicit rather than accidental.

title: Decode external unknown values

title: Use JSON codecs

title: Decode in the Effect error channel

title: Keep encoded and decoded types distinct

title: Represent continuous data as Stream
instruction: Use Stream for ongoing or incremental effectful data sources instead of hand-managed event loops and native stream plumbing.

title: Preserve backpressure

exceptions: A small finite array is not automatically a stream. Preserve ordering, buffering, error behavior, and resource ownership when migrating a pipeline.

title: Avoid unbounded collection

exceptions: A small finite array is not automatically a stream. Preserve ordering, buffering, error behavior, and resource ownership when migrating a pipeline.

title: Scope stream resources

exceptions: A small finite array is not automatically a stream. Preserve ordering, buffering, error behavior, and resource ownership when migrating a pipeline.

title: Use a fitting Sink

exceptions: A small finite array is not automatically a stream. Preserve ordering, buffering, error behavior, and resource ownership when migrating a pipeline.

title: Preserve stream exits
instruction: Propagate failures and interruption through the stream pipeline. Clean up upstream work when the consumer stops early.
exceptions: A small finite array is not automatically a stream. Preserve ordering, buffering, error behavior, and resource ownership when migrating a pipeline.

title: Use Ref for shared state
